10.1002_adma.72638: In inverted perovskite solar cells, self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) employed as hole‐transport layers can significantly improve device performance, with power conversion efficiencies currently exceeding 27%. However, the non‐uniform and weak adsorption of SAMs on metal oxide substrates leads to severe non‐radiative recombination at the buried interface, which remains a critical bottleneck for long‐term operational and thermal stability. In this study, heptafluorobutyramide (HA) or heptafluorobutylimidamide (HM) is introduced into MeO‑4PACz to tailor its adsorption on the NiO x surface. Leveraging multiple hydrogen‑bonding interactions between HM and MeO‑4PACz, the resulting SAMs adopt an inclined orientation of approximately 60° relative to the NiO x surface. This configuration increases the proportion of Ni 3 + on the substrate and raises the surface coverage from 0.912 to 1.236. It also effectively passivates undercoordinated Pb defects at the buried interface, enhances interfacial uniformity, and suppresses non‑radiative recombination. Using a vacuum‑flash processing method, HM‑optimized devices achieve a champion efficiency of 26.99% (certified steady‑state efficiency 26.62%) and reach 20.36% on a large‑area module with an active area of 809.69 cm 2 . Moreover, small‐area devices retained 92% and 87% of their initial efficiency after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking at 25°C and 60°C, respectively.
10.1002_smll.75564: Extending the cycle life of LiCoO 2 (LCO) cathodes under elevated cutoff voltages remains a critical challenge for lithium‐ion batteries, as accelerated degradation is often governed by reaction heterogeneity and interfacial instability. Herein, we report a composite cathode composed of micron‐sized LCO and nanoscale LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 , in which LMFP functions as a kinetically robust and electrochemically active component. Without invoking specific heterostructures, the optimized composite exhibits outstanding cycling stability at 4.45 V, retaining 94.2% of its initial capacity after 300 cycles at 1 C/1 C and 91.4% after 300 cycles at 3 C/3 C. Even at 4.6 V, the composite consistently outperforms pristine LCO. Importantly, pouch cells paired with a prelithiated silicon‐carbon anode deliver an energy density of 250 Wh kg −1 and maintain 81.8% capacity retention over 400 cycles. These results highlight a practical composite cathode strategy for prolonging the service life of LCO‐based batteries within realistic voltage windows, offering a scalable pathway toward durable high‐energy lithium‐ion systems.
10.1007_s00604-025-07083-3: The escalating global prevalence of allergies presents a substantial public health challenge. Immunoglobulin E (IgE) serves as a key biomarker for allergic diseases, often measured in blood serum by ELISA immunoassays. Despite recent interest in minimally invasive sampling of biological fluids, the low sample volumes and IgE concentrations demand highly sensitive methodologies, typically confined to centralized laboratories. In this article, a decentralizable approach based on competitive immunoassays using Pd nanocluster (PdNCs)-labelled antibodies for electrochemical detection is proposed. With this aim, PdNCs were successfully bioconjugated with an anti-hIgE antibody to perform competitive immunoassays. To improve the analytical capabilities of the methodology, disposable screen-printed carbon electrodes with dual working electrodes were used for enhancing precision. Prior electrodeposition of PdNCs at − 0.6 V for 90 s significantly improved sensitivity (7.1 µA g ng⁻1) and lowered the limit of detection (LoD) to 0.3 ng g⁻1 for PdNCs determination. The use of PdNCs as labels resulted in an improvement in the LoD for IgE determination. Calibration curves performed using competitive immunoassays for IgE determination, ranging from 10−5 to 102 ng g−1, demonstrated sensitivity comparable to high-tech methods, with a LoD of 0.008 ng g−1 for electrochemical measurements. Bimodal detection of Pd (linear sweep voltammetry and inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry) in various biological fluids (saliva, tears, nasal exudate, capillary blood, and blood serum) revealed significant differences in IgE levels between allergic and non-allergic individuals. Notably, capillary blood correlated strongly with serum blood, and a certain correlation has also been found with nasal exudate. The electrochemical approach, combining sensitivity and precision with non-invasive sampling, offers a simplified alternative for IgE determination in allergic disease. Graphical Abstract
10.1016_j.ijrefrig.2026.107068: • A mobile two-phase direct cooling system was modeled as BTMS under typical driving cycles. • The inclusion of PCM attached to the battery evaporator was proposed and modeled. • Low-GWP refrigerants performed comparably to R-134a after compressor stroke adjustment. • The system with PCM saved 3% of battery power under the NEDC driving cycle. Electric vehicles (EVs) are viable alternatives to internal combustion engine vehicles. However, the driving range limitations remain a key challenge. Effective thermal management of batteries and cabin air-conditioning systems can help to address these challenges. Proper battery thermal management systems (BTMS) enhance battery performance, extend battery lifespan, and enable faster charging. Moreover, improvements occur when the BTMS is integrated with a phase-change material (PCM) module consisting of a thermal energy storage system. In this study, the transient behavior of a direct cooling system with a PCM in an EV was modeled using an implicit approach. The model includes a compressor, condenser, and two evaporators for cabin and battery bank cooling, with a thermostatic expansion valve and dodecanoic acid as PCM. Four refrigerants were assessed: R-134a, R-1234yf, R-1234ze, and R-32. Experimental testing on a chassis dynamometer provided the heat transfer coefficients and thermal capacities of the system components. The simulation runs used constant and New European Driving Cycle (NEDC)-based battery power inputs. The results indicated that low Global-Warming Potential (GWP) refrigerants performed comparably to R-134a when the compressor displacement was adjusted, except for R-32, which exhibited a lower refrigeration capability. The system with PCM conserved 3% of the battery power, potentially extending the vehicle range by 1.99%.
10.1016_j.isci.2025.112133: SUMMARYThe transition metal oxide CoO has garnered significant attention as a potential anode material for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), owing to its impressive theoretical specific capacity and high energy density. However, pristine CoO often suffer from structural collapse under high current densities, particularly during extended cycling, which results in decreased conductivity, volume expansion, and subsequent capacity fade. To address these challenges, we have developed a method to in-situ grow octahedral CoO nanoparticles on layered two-dimensional MoB MBene through a solvothermal approach. The strategic choice of ethanol as the dispersion solvent effectively mitigates surface oxidation of MoB MBene, thereby facilitating high-speed Li+ and electron transport channels. Furthermore, the matching layer spacing and the formation of a heterojunction between CoO and MoB MBene effectively accommodate the volume expansion of CoO during cycling. As anticipated, the CoO/MoB MBene anode demonstrates exceptional performance, with a specific capacity of 819.8 mAh/g after 200 cycles at 100 mA/g—a remarkable 2.58-fold improvement compared to pristine CoO. Even at a higher current density of 1000 mA/g, the composite maintains a capacity of 601.3 mAh/g after 600 charge-discharge cycles, while the pristine material only retains 142.4 mAh/g. This breakthrough is attributed to the combination of mild chemical scissor etching and solvothermal synthesis, which enables the design and preparation of high-capacitance energy storage materials for LIB anodes. Our findings suggest that the CoO/MoB MBene composite holds great promise for enhancing the performance of LIBs and may pave the way for the development of advanced anode materials.
10.1021_acs.analchem.5c02691: A laser sensor system was developed to be employed in power plants and specifically engineered for high-particulate and high-temperature environments to be applicable for the online monitoring of hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) and carbon monoxide (CO) near the furnace water wall. The system was designed based on frequency division multiplexing (FDM) and tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS). A corrosion-resistant Herriott multipass cell was designed to withstand temperatures of up to 120 °C while providing an 18 m optical path length. The sensor system exhibits measurement uncertainties below 1.5% and 2% under mechanical vibration testing and thermal cycling testing. Allan variance analysis revealed minimum detection limits of 111 ppb for H 2 S and 116 ppb for CO, achievable at integration times of 178 and 144 s, respectively. Long-term field validation in a coal-fired boiler included multipoint sampling to assess the sensor system performance, simultaneously analyzing water-wall combustion dynamics and evaluating corrosion propensity.
10.1039_d5mh00417a: This paper describes a detailed simulation approach to simulate the redox process on CuZn alloys, bridging traditional calculations with large-scale, multi-step processes. Through comprehensive redox process simulation, we identify the specific active sites for ethanol production on redox-treated CuZn surfaces while establishing a universally applicable simulation method.
10.1039_d5ta10427k: This work clarifies the pH-dependent deposition and dissolution of MnO 2 in aqueous electrolytes using in situ EQCM. It shows that proton-coupled redox processes and interfacial pH govern MnO 2 growth, stability, and dissolution behavior.
10.1109_tte.2026.3683068: Accurate estimation of the state of health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) of second-life lithium-ion batteries (SL-LIBs) retired from electric vehicles is critical for their safe reuse in energy storage systems. Existing methods often face challenges such as limited labeled data and poor generalization across diverse working conditions. To address these limitations, we propose a co-estimation framework for SL-LIBs that integrates self-supervised auxiliary learning, gradient adversarial training, and uncertainty calibration within a multi-task learning architecture. The framework introduces the discharge capacity change rate as an auxiliary label to enrich degradation information, while gradient adversarial training mitigates gradient interference between tasks. Additionally, predictive uncertainty is quantified using Monte Carlo Dropout and further calibrated through isotonic regression to enhance reliability. Extensive experiments on a self-tested dataset of 84 SL-LIBs demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a mean absolute error of 0.0089 for SOH and 67 cycles for RUL, reducing the best published baseline by 41% and 39%, respectively.
